texts.facts: 1 1. Briefly stated, the case of the prosecution is that the complainant Rajpal has a house of two and a half floors at no. C- 237, Gali No. 1, Pratap Nagar, Delhi. He used to reside on the ground floor whereas three tenants used to reside on the first floor and another tenant used to reside on the top floor. It is alleged that on 09.05.2010 at about 09:30 AM, while the complainant was sitting outside his house, his daughter came and informed him that a gas cylinder has caught fire in the house of accused Subodh, who was his tenant. He rushed to the house of the accused and found that his wife was inside the room and the gas cylinder was on fire. They tried to put out the fire but suddenly an explosion occurred in the cylinder, due to which the walls of the room got damaged, which also damaged the neighbouring houses. As a result, the victim Harpal, who was the neighbour of the complainant, lost his life and other persons suffered grievous and simple injuries. The allegations of the prosecution are that due to negligence in taking care of the cylinder, the incident occurred. As such, it is alleged that the accused has committed the offences punishable under Section 285/337/338/304A of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter, "IPC"), for which FIR No. 86/2010 was registered at the Harsh Vihar Police Station, New Delhi. 2. After registration of the FIR, the Investigating Officer (hereinafter, "IO") undertook investigation and on culmination of the same, the charge-sheet against the accused was filed. After DEV CHAUDHARY CHAUDHARY Date: 2023.08.21 15:29:01 +0530 taking cognizance of the offence, the accused was summoned to face trial. 3. On his appearance, a copy of charge-sheet was supplied to him in terms of Section 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter, "CrPC"). On finding a prima facie case against the accused, notice of accusation under Sections 285/337/338/304A IPC was framed against the accused Subodh. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Baby (PW1) is one of the injured, who deposed on oath that on 09.05.2010 at around 9 pm, she was inside her house, when she heard a noise from the upper floor of her house. She deposed that she went to her father and her parents then went to the house of the accused. She also went there and her parents tried to douse the fire. However, there was a loud explosion thereafter, and she lost consciousness. 5.1. In her cross examination, Baby (PW1) stated that she alongwith her parents tried to douse the fire. She stated that she does not know the contents of the documents on which her signatures were obtained by the police. 6. Raj Pal (PW2) is the complainant, who deposed on oath that he does not remember the month and year of the incident. DEV CHAUDHARY He deposed that he was sitting outside his house, when the wife of accused Subodh, namely Reena came from her house on the first floor and raised an alarm by saying that the cylinder has caught fire. He deposed that they rushed to the first floor and saw that a gas cylinder of 5l had caught fire. He deposed that he asked the persons gathered there to leave and, in the meantime, the cylinder burst. Due to the explosion, they sustained injuries and the walls of the house fell. He identified the accused and the case property. 6.1. In cross examination, Rajpal (PW2) stated that his house was constructed without any permission from the MCD. He stated that he did not remember the names of the other tenants. He stated that the family of the other tenants on the first floor did not suffer any injuries in the incident. He stated that he did not call the fire brigade and accepted that the accused was not present inside the house at the time of the incident. He stated that the police did not record statements of any witnesses in his presence. 7. SI Jai Bhagwan (PW5) is the first IO, who deposed on oath that the investigation of this case was marked to him. He went to the spot and came to know that a gas cylinder has caught fire. He deposed that he recorded statement of the complainant on the next day and registered the FIR. He deposed about preparing the site plan, obtaining the MLCs of victims, getting post mortem of the deceased conducted etc. He also identified the spot by looking at the photographs. 7.1. In cross examination, SI Jai Bhagwan (PW5) stated there were three tenants living at the premises in question. One was Mr. Harpal and he did not remember the names of other two tenants. DEV CHAU CHAUDHARY Date 15:2 He stated that the fire was extinguished by fire tenders. He admitted that complainant tried to extinguish the fire by pouring water on the cylinder. On Court questioning, he stated that he did not State vs . on 21 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68747838/ 3 record statement of the firemen and did not send the gas cylinder for examination. He stated that he did not seize any documents to show that the accused had purchased the cylinder. 8. Rest of the prosecution witnesses supported the case of the prosecution and proved the documents mentioned in the Table above. 9. Thereafter, before the start of defence evidence, in order to allow the accused to personally explain the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against him, the statement of the accused was recorded without oath under Section 281 read with Section 313 CrPC. In reply, the accused Subodh stated he is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present. Pursuant thereto, he stated that he does not wish to lead any evidence in his defence.
texts.arguments: 11. It is argued by the learned APP for the State that all the ingredients of the offence are fulfilled in the present case. He has argued that the factum of incident is proved. Further, the injured and eye-witnesses have deposed about the incident in detail and the other documentary evidence on record has corroborated the version of the prosecution witnesses. He contends that the prosecution has DEV CHAUDHARY CHAUDHARY Date: 2023.08.21 15:29:31 +0530 proved the offences beyond reasonable doubt. As such, it is prayed that the accused be punished for the said offences. 12. Per contra, learned counsel for the accused has argued that the State has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ld. counsel has argued that the prosecution witnesses have not deposed against the accused and the investigation in the case is faulty. It is argued that the case has not been proved by the prosecution and the prosecution has failed to discharge the burden cast upon it. As such, it is prayed that the accused be acquitted for the said offences. ANALYSIS - 13. The accused has been charged for the offences of negligent conduct with fire or combustible matter (S. 285 IPC), causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others (S. 337 IPC), causing hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others (S. 338 IPC), and causing death by a rash or negligent act (S. 304A IPC) in the present case. The prosecution has to prove that the accused did an act so rashly or negligently with respect to fire or combustible matter in his possession so as to endanger human life etc. Under Section 337/338/304A IPC, hurt and death of the victim should be caused in pursuance of such rash or negligent act of the accused. All 776 the term "rashness" was interpreted to mean commission of an act with indifference or recklessness towards the consequences of such act. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rathnashalvan vs. State of Karnataka (2007) 3 SCC 474 has observed, inter alia, as under-: "7. .... Culpable negligence lies in the failure to exercise reasonable and proper care and the extent of its reasonableness will always depend upon the circumstances of each case. Rashness means doing an act with the consciousness of a risk that evil consequences will follow but with the hope that it will not. Negligence is a breach of duty imposed by law. In criminal cases, the amount and degree of negligence are determining factors. A question whether the accused's conduct amounted to culpable rashness or negligence depends directly on the question as to what is the amount of care and circumspection which a prudent and reasonable man would consider it to be sufficient considering all the circumstances of the case. Criminal rashness means hazarding a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is dangerous or wanton and the further knowledge that it may cause injury but done without any intention to cause injury or knowledge that it would probably be caused. 8. As noted above, "rashness" consists in hazarding a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is so, and that it may cause injury. Criminal negligence on the other hand, is the gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which, having regard to all the circumstances out of which the charge has arisen it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted." Similar observations were made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushil Ansal vs. CBI (2014) 6 SCC 173. The standard of negligence was discussed in the said case, by observing, inter alia, as under-: "58. In the case of "negligence" the courts have favoured a meaning which implies a gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual DEV Negligence has been understood to be an omission to do something which a reasonable man guided upon those considerations which ordinarily regulate the conduct of human affairs, would do, or doing something which a prudent and reasonable person would not do. The imputability in the case of negligence arises from the neglect of the civil duty of State vs . on 21 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68747838/ 5 circumspection." Thus, rashness implies doing an act despite the consciousness that it might result in injuries. As to what is meant by causa causans we may gainfully refer to Black's Law Dictionary (5th Edn.) which defines that expression as under: "Causa causans.--The immediate cause; the last link in the chain of causation." The Advance Law Lexicon edited by Justice Chandrachud, former Chief Justice of India defines causa causans as follows: "Causa causans.--The immediate cause as opposed to a remote cause; the 'last link in the chain of causation'; the real effective cause of damage."
